note: Every set below is exact. The failing side reports these ids and no others, and the corrected side reports the residual set and no others. SHAPE005 is in every set because the baseline reports the release it claims to be, which is information rather than a defect.

pairs.name: debug-display-on
pairs.summary: WP_DEBUG is on and errors are rendered into the page instead of a log.

pairs.name: debug-log-in-web-root
pairs.summary: The debug log path is built with a function call and lands inside the web root, where a request can read it.

pairs.name: maintenance-file-left-behind
pairs.summary: An update stopped part way and left the file that shows every visitor the maintenance notice.

pairs.name: uploads-php-shell
pairs.summary: A PHP file with a double extension sitting in the media directory.

pairs.name: uploads-htaccess-php-handler
pairs.summary: The uploads directory is configured to execute PHP.

pairs.name: output-before-open-tag
pairs.summary: A blank line before the opening PHP tag in the theme, which breaks every redirect and cookie.

pairs.name: obfuscated-mu-loader
pairs.summary: A must-use plugin that loads before everything and hides what it does.

pairs.name: mu-loader-from-uploads
pairs.summary: A must-use plugin whose body is loaded from the uploads directory, so anything that can write a file decides what runs.

pairs.name: unknown-dropin
pairs.summary: A file in wp-content named like a drop-in, which WordPress does not actually load.

pairs.name: htaccess-redirect-loop
pairs.summary: One rule forces https and another names an http target, which is a redirect loop in the browser.

pairs.name: canonical-host-rules
pairs.summary: Two canonical host rules that each rewrite away from the host the other one wants.

pairs.name: rogue-root-php
pairs.summary: A PHP file at the web root that no WordPress release ships.
